1.why: Four adjectives of physical bearing/quality, no overlap tight enough to be a duplicate. Pick is a hunch that 'agile' is the more testable word, not elimination.

2.why: Four transitive verbs that all take a law/practice as object; each supports a plausible stem. Pick is a hunch.

3.why: Four adjectives naming distinct failings (attention, coordination, effort, nerve). 'careless'/'clumsy' are near but not interchangeable. Pick is a hunch.

4.why: Four nouns that are all genuine plant/growth inputs, so any of them answers some stem. Pick is a hunch.

5.why: Four speech verbs with different attitudes; all legal. Pick is a hunch.

6.why: Two physical measures and two character traits; a person-subject stem makes the traits legal and an object-subject stem makes the measures legal, so none is dead on arrival. Pick is a hunch.

7.why: A and D are antonyms rather than duplicates, and B/C describe different states of the same planting. All four legal. Pick is a hunch.

8.why: Four intransitive verbs of change over time, mutually exclusive in direction. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

9.why: Four nouns attachable to a book/map/document; 'scale' is the odd register but a map stem makes it fully legal. Pick is a hunch.

10.why: Four adjectives describing how something was arrived at; B and C are opposed, A and D are unrelated causes. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

11.why: Four adjectives of waiting/attitude. 'watchful' and 'apprehensive' differ in affect, not synonymous. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

12.why: Four transitive verbs of effect on a person, each a distinct effect. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

13.why: Three defect adjectives plus one decorative one ('ornate'); register differs but a description stem makes it legal. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

14.why: Four unrelated adjectives, no pair close enough to collide. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

15.why: Four adjectives predicable of a document/map/sign, mutually distinct. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

16.why: Two-blank item; every pair is adjective..adjective and internally coherent, including 'precise . . . silent'. Without the stem no pair is excluded. Pick is a hunch that the contrastive pair is keyed.

17.why: Four phrases about money behaviour: A is opposed to B, C and D are distinct habits. All legal. Pick is a hunch that a miserliness headword is the target.

18.why: Four adjectives predicable of a task, each naming a different kind of difficulty. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

19.why: All four share the un- prefix, which is a cross-item shape but not an illegality: the four stems are unrelated and none duplicates another. Pick is a hunch.

20.why: Four adjectives about cost, room, pattern and pace; no overlap. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

21.why: Four adjectives qualifying an action/measure along different axes. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

22.why: Four adjectives of manner/disposition, mutually distinct. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

23.why: Four nouns; 'record' and 'origin' are unrelated senses, no collision. All legal. Pick is a hunch.

24.why: All four are un- adjectives and 'uncorroborated' sits a register above the rest, but high register is not illegality and none duplicates another. Pick is a hunch, and it is exactly the hunch this stage warns about ('the hard word is the answer'), so it carries no weight.

25.why: D 'replaced' is the wrong form given the other three. A 'totals' and B 'means' are unambiguously present third-person singular verbs (or plural/mass nouns); 'replaced' is past tense/participle and is not a noun, so neither a present-tense verb frame nor a noun frame can accommodate it while the others fit. No headword or sentence makes it the answer alongside A and B. Remaining pick among A/B/C is a hunch, not elimination.
